2607.08961.title: NL-PAC: Specification Ambiguity and Certified Minimax Risk Floors in LLM-Mediated Supervision
2607.08961.paper_summary: Large language models increasingly provide labels, evaluations, and feedback for tasks specified in natural language. When a specification admits multiple readings but the supervision channel does not reveal which is operative, additional labels reduce sampling error without resolving the resulting identification problem. We introduce Natural Language PAC (NL-PAC), a framework that uses a fixed model's thresholded decoding law to define admissible labels and candidate targets. The probability that multiple labels are admissible equals the diameter of the pointwise-admissible target class, and under target-blind supervision every learner incurs worst-case risk of at least half this diameter, at every sample size; the exact randomized minimax risk over this class is attained by a data-independent strategy. Finite-sample confidence bounds make these quantities certifiable from held-out unlabeled inputs. In a frozen Qwen~2.5--3B audit, one prespecified prompt yields a positive model-relative certificate, whereas a paraphrase and exact-rule controls yield zero. A held-out bridge audit finds that supplied candidate reading clauses fail the admissibility condition needed to transfer the certificate to coherent readings. The guarantee is specific to the audited model, prompt, threshold, and input distribution; extending it to human interpretations requires external validation.
2607.08961.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地為自然語言指定的任務提供標籤、評估和反饋。當一個規範允許多種解讀，但監督通道並未揭示哪一種是有效的時，額外的標籤會減少取樣誤差，但無法解決由此產生的識別問題。我們引入自然語言PAC（NL-PAC），這是一個使用固定模型的閾值解碼法則來定義可接受標籤和候選目標的框架。多個標籤可接受的概率等於逐點可接受目標類的直徑，而在目標盲監督下，每個學習者在每個樣本大小上都會承擔至少一半這個直徑的最壞情況風險；這個類別的精確隨機最小最大風險是由一種與數據無關的策略達成的。有限樣本置信界使這些量能從保留的未標記輸入中得到認證。在一個冷凍的Qwen~2.5--3B審計中，一個預先指定的提示產生了一個正面的模型相對證書，而一個改寫和精確規則的控制則產生了零的結果。一個保留的橋接審計發現，提供的候選閱讀條款未能滿足轉移證書到連貫閱讀所需的可接受性條件。這一保證是特定於被審計的模型、提示、閾值和輸入分佈；將其擴展到人類解釋需要外部驗證。
2607.08961.author: Berkay Anahtarci et.al.
